note: The rungs. ms = metres per second. Where a rung is arithmetic off a published measurement, show is the arithmetic and src points at the measurement.

rungs.name: The ground under the house
rungs.say: The Atlantic gets wider about as fast as a fingernail grows. You have been movin' this whole time and nobody spilled their coffee.

rungs.name: A racin' snail
rungs.say: That is the course record at Congham, and the snail that set it was named Archie. Thirteen inches, two minutes, downhill in spirit only.

rungs.name: A body walkin'
rungs.show: 3.5 ft/s, the figure the crosswalk timer is set by
rungs.say: Every WALK light in the country is timed off this number. When the hand starts blinkin' early, the argument is with a federal table.

rungs.name: Usain Bolt, flat out
rungs.show: peak over the 60–80 m split; the whole 100 m averaged 10.44 m/s
rungs.say: Fastest a human body has been measured movin' under its own steam. He was not goin' that fast at the gun and he was slowin' at the tape.

rungs.name: A cheetah, hunting
rungs.show: measured on wild cheetahs wearin' a collar, in the hunt
rungs.say: Twice Bolt and change. The collar caught 25.9 m/s over a single stride — not a zoo sprint down a straight lane, but a turn-and-burn after dinner.

rungs.name: Pickup on the interstate
rungs.say: You beat the cheetah in third gear and it cost you a gallon every eighteen miles or so.

rungs.name: A peregrine, stooping
rungs.show: 242 mph, clocked off a skydiver's meter
rungs.say: Ken Franklin jumped out of the plane with the bird and they fell together so the speed could be read. Fastest anything alive has been measured goin'.

rungs.name: ThrustSSC, on the salt
rungs.show: 763.035 mph, two runs inside an hour, averaged
rungs.say: Andy Green, Black Rock Desert, 15 October 1997 — 1.9 m/s under the speed of sound on the salt that day only because the desert air was cold. First car to go supersonic, and still the record, which tells you somethin' about how hard the next mile an hour is.

rungs.name: Sound, in the air out front
rungs.show: dry air at 20 °C; colder air is slower
rungs.say: The rung everything else on this page gets measured against. Count the seconds after the flash and divide by three for kilometres, by five for miles.

rungs.name: The tip of a bullwhip
rungs.show: about twice the speed of sound at the tip
rungs.say: The crack is a sonic boom. A whip was the first thing a person ever made go faster than sound, and it was doin' it for centuries before anybody worked out why.

rungs.name: A .30-06, leavin' the muzzle
rungs.show: 2,800 ft/s, 150-grain factory load
rungs.say: Two and a half times the speed of sound before it clears the porch rail. The crack you hear downrange is the bullet's own boom, not the powder.

rungs.name: An SR-71, in a straight line
rungs.show: 3,529.56 km/h, the standin' record for an air-breathin' aeroplane
rungs.say: Eldon Joersz and George Morgan, 28 July 1976. Fifty years on, nothin' with a person in it and an air intake has gone quicker and had it certified.

rungs.name: The X-15, with the rocket lit
rungs.show: Mach 6.7, 4,520 mph
rungs.say: Pete Knight, 3 October 1967. The paint burned off. The airframe came home warped and that airplane never flew again.

rungs.name: The space station, goin' around
rungs.show: √(GM/r) at 420 km up
rungs.say: Sunrise every ninety-two minutes. It is not up there because it went up. It is up there because it is goin' sideways this fast and keeps missin'.

rungs.name: Quittin' the Earth entirely
rungs.show: √(2GM/R) at the ground, air not counted
rungs.say: Throw somethin' this fast and straight up and it does not come back down. Ever. No engine needed after the throw.

rungs.name: Voyager 1, still leavin'
rungs.show: about 61,000 km/h away from the Sun
rungs.say: Launched in 1977, out past the edge of the Sun's wind, and still talkin' back on a transmitter weaker than a refrigerator bulb.

rungs.name: This whole planet, orbitin'
rungs.show: the Earth's mean orbital speed
rungs.say: Sittin' on the porch, you are doin' this. Sixty-seven thousand miles an hour and the sweet tea does not slosh.

rungs.name: The Parker Solar Probe, at the bottom
rungs.show: about 692,000 km/h at closest approach, 24 December 2024
rungs.say: Fastest thing people have ever built. The Sun did most of the work — the probe fell, the way anything falls, and the Sun is a long way down.

rungs.name: The Sun, haulin' the lot of us
rungs.show: around the centre of the Milky Way
rungs.say: One lap takes about 230 million years. Last time we were here, the dinosaurs had not started.

rungs.name: Light
rungs.show: exact, by definition
rungs.say: Not measured any more. Fixed. The metre is defined as how far light goes in 1/299,792,458 of a second, so the number cannot be wrong — the ruler moves instead.
